_desc: Comprehensive mobile+team plane test. Static net {S1(home),S2} + off-grid team {TeamA,TeamB,TeamC} (real crypto identities via per-node seeds) + a home-registered mobile {M1}, co-located so statics HEAR the team beacons. Checks: (#1) team beacons DON'T leak into a static id_bind, (#2) plaintext team DM, (#3) ENCRYPTED team DM via team-scoped WANT_PUBKEY (reqpubkey -> peer_key_cached -> send_hashx), (#4) static->registered-mobile via home last-mile, (#5) registered-mobile->static with e2e reverse-ack, plus team-DAD, team channel + containment, team-DM containment, mobile-id non-leak. Team key_hash32 are seed-derived (LE(ed_pub[:4])): TeamA a1*32=0x2215F68F, TeamB b2*32=0x8B94BBD1, TeamC c3*32=0x38E8B9F4. Pairs with the s18 byte-identity tripwire.

commands._c: #3 step1: TeamA fetches TeamC's E2E pubkey on-air (team-scoped WANT_PUBKEY). ★ PLANE 2026-07-31 (§sim-plane-parity B3): the trailing `-t` is now REQUIRED for a team-scoped WANT_PUBKEY. The sim used to leave Command.u.resolve.plane at 0 (AUTO) for reqpubkey while the console assigns `team ? TEAM : GLOBAL` (console_parse.cpp:190) — the fourth and last AUTO divergence on a Command field. ⚠ WITHOUT `-t` this query is GLOBAL, and on this homeless off-grid member NO h_tx is emitted at all, so TeamA never caches TeamC's pubkey and the sealed DM below never decrypts — 3 asserts fail, including #35's exact static count (a GLOBAL WANT_PUBKEY floods the STATIC plane and pulls S2 in, 6 -> 7). ★ And the `-t` alone was a NO-OP before the fix: scan_hex32 breaks on the space, so the flag was silently swallowed — which is why this survived four slices of plane work.

#2 plaintext team DM (by teammate hash). ★ PLANE 2026-07-28 (§sim-plane-parity): the trailing `-t` is now REQUIRED for a team-plane DM. The sim's plain DM verbs used to leave Command.u.send.plane at 0 (AUTO); they now emit GLOBAL, mirroring lib/console/console_parse.cpp:259 (`team ? TEAM : GLOBAL`), the ONLY plane assignment on real firmware. Without `-t` this send is GLOBAL, and §6.4/§18 then force the STATIC _rt (node_routing.cpp:22) and skip the team hash-locate cascade (node_hashlocate.cpp:1021) — exactly what metal does. ★ send_hashx (the SEALED team DM below) carries `-t` for the same reason: it is the THIRD DM-producing site in NodeRuntimeWrapper.cpp and had no `-t` at all before this slice, so a sealed team DM could only ever ride AUTO. The two static-facing lines (send_hash 11110060 static_to_mobile, send_e2e S2 mobile_to_static) stay PLAIN deliberately — their intent is the global/home plane and they are unaffected by the flip.
#3 step2: TeamA sends an ENCRYPTED (sealed) team DM to TeamC
#4 static S2 -> registered mobile M1 (by hash; S1 home last-miles)
#5 registered mobile M1 -> static S2 with e2e-ACK (reverse leg)

§team-parity T5 #1 — THE TEAM BIDI PLANE EXISTS: a team CTS / heard-set hit records a CONFIRMED verdict against a team_local_id (241 = TeamA). Pre-T5 this event could not exist on the team plane at all — note_link_confirmed had no team arm, and T2 marked the site ✖ twice ('there is nothing to write it to').

T5 #2 — TeamB positively establishes that its DIRECT link to TeamA (241) is ONE-WAY, from TeamA's COMPLETE heard-set page. This is T3's heard_set_complete-on-team-beacons finally having a consumer (T3 recorded it as '0/36 BY CONSTRUCTION, T5 owns consumption').

★★ T5 #3 — MUTUAL RECOGNITION, which is spec §3/T5's literal purpose ('what would have let 213 and 174 recognise that their direct link is one-way'). The OTHER endpoint independently reaches the same verdict about TeamB (143). Pairs with #2 so neither can pass by the mechanism simply not running.

★★ T5 #4 — THE ROUTING CONSEQUENCE, and the ONLY path-selection change T5 makes anywhere in the corpus: with the direct hop demoted by bidi_penalty_one_way_q4, TeamB commits to the 2-HOP path to 241 via TeamC (224) as PRIMARY. Pre-T5 the identical candidate installed as 'alt' and the one-way direct hop stayed primary. If this line reads slot:alt again, effective_score has stopped consuming the team bidi state.

T5 #5 — the TRANSITIVE half (candidate_degraded's team arm): TeamB now advertises the one-way team route as `degraded` in its beacon route page, which the team plane could not do before (it was wire-only). NB `degraded` is a gossip bit — no routing decision reads it on either plane.
T5 #6 — RECOVERY is reachable, not a one-way ratchet (MF6/§7): a later confirm clears the one_way verdict...
... and it fans out through team_resort_routes_through with T5's own reason string, so a bidi rerank is distinguishable from a liveness-tier rerank in the stream.

★★★ T5 #7 — INVARIANT I8 / I2, THE ACCEPTANCE CRITERION: a STATIC node never takes the team bidi arm. Absence assertions, and per the T8 rule they are PAIRED with the presences above (#1/#2/#3 require the team-plane verdicts to exist), so 'zero on the statics' cannot be satisfied by the mechanism not running.

T5 #8 — the same invariant stated on the ID rather than the plane tag, which is the form that catches a team local id reaching the node_id-indexed _link_bidi[256] by ANY route (the exact leak T3 measured on the pre-fix arm: statics writing _link_bidi[100]/[200]/[98]). 143/241/224 are this scenario's three team local ids.

T5 #9 — STATIC-PLANE INVARIANCE, pinned as an exact count: T5 adds ZERO static bidi events. These two numbers are pre-T5 values and have nothing to do with T5 — that is the point; they are the tightest available statement that the slice did not touch the static plane. If a future slice legitimately changes static beacon timing, s22 re-anchors anyway and these move with it.
